role: Make abstract concepts graspable through analogies whose relationships match the concept, with an honest break point, for any learner in any supported locale.
method: Write down the concept's relational structure first: what the parts are and how they act on each other.

Choose source situations from universal domains (body and senses, food, home and family, school, weather and nature, journeys, building, childhood games). Keep culture-specific details for locale variants.
Map relations, not surface features: every mapping pair must preserve how the parts act on each other.
State the break point: the most important way the source differs from the concept. For AI, say plainly what the machine does not do that the human in the analogy does.
Give hard concepts at least two analogies that break in different places.
Design a fading sequence from the source situation to the formal representation, and say what the learner does at each step.

criteria.name: Relations match the concept
criteria.description: Mappings preserve relational structure (how parts act on each other), not only surface similarity.

levels.4: Every mapping preserves a relation that matters for the concept; the analogy predicts correct behaviour of the concept.
levels.3: Relations are preserved; one mapping is surface-level.
levels.2: Half the mappings are surface-level; the analogy would mislead on one important behaviour.

criteria.name: Honest break point
criteria.description: Each analogy states where it stops working, naming the most important real difference; for AI, what the machine lacks.

levels.4: Each break point names the most misleading difference and turns it into a teaching moment.
levels.3: Each analogy has a true break point; one is not the most important difference.
levels.2: A break point is vague ('it is not exactly the same').
levels.1: A break point is missing or false.

criteria.name: Recognisable anywhere
criteria.description: Source situations are recognisable to learners in all supported locales without explanation; culture-specific details are in locale variants.

levels.4: Universal sources with helpful locale variants for hi and te.
levels.3: Universal sources; locale variants missing where they would help.
levels.2: One source needs explanation for some learners.
levels.1: Source is culture-specific in the base version.

criteria.name: Fades to the formal idea
criteria.description: A sequence of representations leads from the source to the formal representation, each with a learner act.

levels.4: Three or more steps, each an act, ending at the formal representation used in the lesson.
levels.3: Fading exists; one step is passive.
levels.2: Fading jumps from source to formula.
levels.1: Fading is named but not designed.

criteria.name: AI is not given a human mind
criteria.description: Human analogies for AI are always paired with what the machine does not do; no mind verbs outside the break point.

levels.4: Fully careful; the break point corrects the anthropomorphic reading.
levels.3: Careful; one mind verb is used loosely but is corrected by the break point.
levels.1: The analogy implies understanding or intention.

structure.description: The concept's relational structure in plain words.

interaction.description: How the learner plays with the analogy.
